subject: Ambiguous ingest attribution — request for usage evidence and provisional credit
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@edgescale.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeScale Billing <billing@edgescale.io>
Date: 2028-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected Feb 28 consumption spike — asking for breakdown

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Hope you9re well. We noticed a significant token/embedding spike on Feb 28 that pushed us about 3x our normal daily usage (see attached top-level export). The spike appears to show a large number of embed requests coming from prefixes that we believe are internal to our staging/test environment, not production.

We9re trying to understand whether this was an attribution/metering mistake on your side (e.g., mis-tagging, prefix reassignments) or if our side accidentally pushed a backfill. Can you: 1) share the raw request IDs and available telemetry for the window 2028-02-28T02:00:00Z to 2028-02-28T10:00:00Z; 2) flag any evidence of duplicate replays/parallel ingest; and 3) let us know your provisional credit policy while this is investigated?

Attaching: usage_export_20280228.csv (summary)

We9re somewhat time-sensitive as this usage tipped our monthly threshold and triggered an automated billing alert. Appreciate a quick read.

— Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Integrations, EdgeScale
alex.kim@edgescale.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@edgescale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-07T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb 28 consumption spike — asking for breakdown

Hi Alex,

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the export. I9ve looped in Ben (billing) and will get Connor (ingest/ops) to pull the raw request logs for the window you specified.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Ben will confirm provisional credit options after we validate the telemetry (likely a provisional pro-rata credit while we audit).
- Connor, can you pull per-request logs (including prefix, request_id, tenant_tag) for 2028-02-28T02:00:00Z - 2028-02-28T10:00:00Z and look for duplicate UUIDs / replay indicators?
- I'll document findings and propose a remediation/credit calculation by EOD tomorrow.

If you have a few sample request IDs from the CSV that you suspect are misattributed, send them over — it speeds matching.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-07T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: EdgeScale - Feb 28 spike (provisional credit + audit)

Forwarding the EdgeScale report. Quick notes:
- If logs show staging/test traffic labeled under EdgeScale's production tenant, we typically apply a provisional credit equal to the difference between observed usage and their 90th percentile baseline for that period while the audit is in progress.
- We9ll need the per-request evidence to compute the dollar amount.

Connor: attaching the CSV Alex sent and a quick excerpt from our usage exporter (query_log_excerpt.txt). Can you triage? If you confirm a mis-tag/mis-route, please include: the root cause, # of tokens attributable to staging, and recommended remediation to prevent recurrence.

Attachments: usage_export_20280228.csv, query_log_excerpt.txt

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Customer Billing
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@edgescale.io>
Date: 2028-03-09T13:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeScale - Feb 28 spike (provisional credit + audit)

Ben/Marissa — quick preliminary summary after an initial query of the ingest logs and routing table:

Findings (high level):
- Between 2028-02-28T02:14:23Z and 2028-02-28T03:07:10Z there were ~2.8M embed tokens billed to EdgeScale tenant (tenant_id: es-prod-14).
- ~42% of those requests originated from a request prefix we internally label as "int-prefetch-01". That prefix is typically used by EdgeScale for staging, but the tenant tag on those requests was es-prod-14 (production).
- Traces show a new CI job (edge-integration/ci-trigger v3.2) that started at 02:13Z and executed a multi-threaded prefetch that fired the same request batch across three worker processes. The worker traces have distinct worker_ids but identical source_request_ids for ~180k requests — evidence of accidental replay/parallelization at their CI side.

Concrete evidence (excerpt):
> 2028-02-28T02:15:04Z prefix=int-prefetch-01 tenant=es-prod-14 request_id=0a9f3b.. worker_id=7f3c pid=2201 replay_flag=1 tokens=1280
> 2028-02-28T02:15:04Z prefix=int-prefetch-01 tenant=es-prod-14 request_id=0a9f3b.. worker_id=9b1a pid=4412 replay_flag=1 tokens=1280

Recommendation:
1) Attribution correction: We can reclassify requests where the prefix matches EdgeScale9s staging pattern AND the request payload/request_id set appears in more than one worker within a 2s window. These will be flagged as "probable replay — staging origin" and excluded from the production bill.
2) Provisional credit: If you agree, we will apply a temporary credit equal to the token-cost of flagged requests for Feb 28 while we complete a full audit (expected 3 business days).
3) Prevent recurrence: Suggest toggling stricter tenant tagging on CI jobs and adding a client-side dedupe at the job orchestration layer. We can provide a short checklist for your infra team.

I will run a full audit and produce a CSV of request_id rows that we propose to reclassify; will share by tomorrow EOD.

Connor
SRE, Ingest Platform
connor_obrien@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@edgescale.io>, EdgeScale Billing <billing@edgescale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb 28 consumption spike — asking for breakdown

Alex — thanks for your patience. Per Connor's initial audit we9re seeing strong evidence of accidental replay coming from a CI prefetch job that was mis-tagging requests with your production tenant.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@edgescale.io>, EdgeScale Billing <billing@edgescale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb 28 consumption spike — asking for breakdown (continued)

(continued)

Action plan we9re proposing:
- We will produce a CSV of the ~180k request_ids we propose to reclassify as "staging/replay" and exclude from your Feb 28 bill. Connor will attach the CSV to the HubSpot record.
- Ben will apply a provisional credit equal to the token cost of those flagged requests immediately upon your confirmation (we9re estimating the provisional credit at ~$4,200). The credit will be reflected on the next invoice but we can also issue a one-off invoice adjustment if you prefer.
- We will keep the provisional credit in place during the 3-business-day audit window while both sides validate the request_id set. If the audit finds additional items we will adjust accordingly.

Please reply with "AGREE" to proceed with the provisional credit and the reclassification, or ask any clarifying questions. If you9d like, Connor and I can hop on a 20-minute call with your infra lead to walk the logs and share the suggested CI tagging checklist.

DocuSign link (optional authorization to proceed): https://docusign.example/ES-4721-credit-approval

Thanks,
Marissa
